title: Numbers up to 200: Tens and Units
seo_title: Numbers up to 200 – Primary 2 Mathematics Worksheets with Answers (NERDC)
standard_text: Count, read and write numbers up to 200; identify tens and units; compare and order numbers. (summary of the NERDC Primary 2 Mathematics curriculum)
meta_desc: Free Primary 2 maths worksheets on numbers up to 200: tens and units, reading and writing numbers, place value with blocks, and comparing numbers. 100 questions with answers.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • A two-digit number has tens and units. 46 = 4 tens and 6 units.
  • 10 units make 1 ten. 10 tens make 1 hundred.
  • To compare, look at the tens first.

Examples

Example

3 tens and 5 units

30 + 5

Answer: 35

Example

Which is bigger, 58 or 85?

8 tens is more than 5 tens

Answer: 85

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Writing 305 for 3 tens and 5 unitsIt is 35.
Mixing up 58 and 85The first digit is the tens.
Looking at the units firstLook at the tens first.

items.q: What number do the blocks show?
items.e: A rod is 10. A small cube is 1. Count the rods in tens: 10, 20. Then add 5 units: 20 + 5 = 25. Each rod is 10, not 1.

items.q: What number do the blocks show?
items.e: A rod is 10. A small cube is 1. Count the rods in tens: 10, 20, 30. Then add 8 units: 30 + 8 = 38.

items.q: How many straws are there?
items.e: A bundle is 10 straws. Count the bundles in tens: 10, 20, 30, 40. Then add 6 units: 40 + 6 = 46.

items.q: Which matches the blocks?
items.e: Count the rods: 3 tens. Count the small cubes: 6 units. The number is 36.
58 is 5 tens and 8 units. There are 5 tens.
36 is 3 tens and 6 units. There are 6 units.
A rod is 10. A small cube is 1. Count the rods in tens: 10, 20, 30, 40, 50, 60. There are no ones, so write 0 in the units place: 60.

items.q: What is the red digit worth?
items.e: The red 6 is in the tens place. It is worth 6 tens = 60. The digit is 6, but its value is 60.

items.q: How many straws are there?
items.e: A bundle is 10 straws. Count the bundles in tens: 10. Then add 9 units: 10 + 9 = 19.

A has 1 hundred, 7 tens and 5 units: 175. B has 1 hundred, 5 tens and 7 units: 157. Both have 1 hundred. Look at the tens next. 175 has 7 tens and 157 has 5 tens. 7 > 5, so 175 > 157. The ones do not matter.
A has 1 hundred, 2 tens and 3 units: 123. B has 1 hundred, 2 tens and 7 units: 127. Both have 1 hundred and 2 tens. Look at the units. 123 has 3 units and 127 has 7 units. 3 < 7, so 123 < 127.
A has 1 hundred, 9 tens and 1 unit: 191. B has 1 hundred, 9 tens and 2 units: 192. Both have 1 hundred and 9 tens. Look at the units. 191 has 1 one and 192 has 2 units. 1 < 2, so 191 < 192.

A has 1 hundred, 8 tens and 7 units: 187. B has 1 hundred, 7 tens and 8 units: 178. Both have 1 hundred. Look at the tens next. 187 has 8 tens and 178 has 7 tens. 8 > 7, so 187 > 178. The ones do not matter.

items.q: Write the number for A and for B. Which is true?
items.e: A has 1 hundred, 2 tens and 1 unit: 121. B has 1 hundred, 0 tens and 9 units: 109. Both have 1 hundred. Look at the tens next. 121 has 2 tens and 109 has 0 tens. 2 > 0, so 121 > 109. The ones do not matter.
A has 1 hundred, 3 tens and 5 units: 135. B has 1 hundred, 5 tens and 7 units: 157. Both have 1 hundred. Look at the tens next. 135 has 3 tens and 157 has 5 tens. 3 < 5, so 135 < 157.

items.q: Write the number for A and for B. Which is true?
items.e: A has 1 hundred, 0 tens and 0 units: 100. B has 1 hundred, 0 tens and 7 units: 107. Both have 1 hundred and 0 tens. Look at the units. 100 has 0 units and 107 has 7 units. 0 < 7, so 100 < 107.

A has 1 hundred, 7 tens and 4 units: 174. B has 1 hundred, 4 tens and 7 units: 147. Both have 1 hundred. Look at the tens next. 174 has 7 tens and 147 has 4 tens. 7 > 4, so 174 > 147. The ones do not matter.

A has 1 hundred, 6 tens and 5 units: 165. B has 1 hundred, 1 ten and 9 units: 119. Both have 1 hundred. Look at the tens next. 165 has 6 tens and 119 has 1 ten. 6 > 1, so 165 > 119. The ones do not matter.
A has 1 hundred, 8 tens and 5 units: 185. B has 1 hundred, 8 tens and 8 units: 188. Both have 1 hundred and 8 tens. Look at the units. 185 has 5 units and 188 has 8 units. 5 < 8, so 185 < 188.
A has 1 hundred, 6 tens and 3 units: 163. B has 1 hundred, 6 tens and 5 units: 165. Both have 1 hundred and 6 tens. Look at the units. 163 has 3 units and 165 has 5 units. 3 < 5, so 163 < 165.
A big square is 1 hundred. A long rod is 1 ten. A small cube is 1 unit. Count each kind: 1 hundred, 2 tens, 1 unit.
A big square is 1 hundred. A long rod is 1 ten. A small cube is 1 unit. Count each kind: 2 hundreds, 7 tens, 9 units.

items.q: What number do the blocks show?
items.e: Count each kind. 1 hundred = 100. 0 tens = 0. 9 units = 9. 100 + 9 = 109. There are no tens, so write 0 in the tens place.
Each rod is 10. There are 2 rods. 2 tens = 20.
Each rod is 10. There are 4 rods. 4 tens = 40.

items.q: What number do the blocks show?
items.e: Count each kind. 1 hundred = 100. 0 tens = 0. 4 units = 4. 100 + 4 = 104. There are no tens, so write 0 in the tens place.
A big square is 1 hundred. A long rod is 1 ten. A small cube is 1 unit. Count each kind: 2 hundreds, 3 tens, 4 units.
Each rod is 10. There are 5 rods. 5 tens = 50.
Count each kind. 1 hundred = 100. 7 tens = 70. 1 one = 1. 100 + 70 + 1 = 171.
A big square is 1 hundred. A long rod is 1 ten. A small cube is 1 unit. Count each kind: 2 hundreds, 5 tens, 8 units.
A big square is 1 hundred. A long rod is 1 ten. A small cube is 1 unit. Count each kind: 4 hundreds, 3 tens, 6 units.
Each rod is 10. There are 5 rods. 5 tens = 50.

items.q: What are the ten rods worth in all?
items.e: Each rod is 10. There are 2 rods. 2 tens = 20.

items.q: What number do the blocks show?
items.e: Count each kind. 1 hundred = 100. 0 tens = 0. 3 units = 3. 100 + 3 = 103. There are no tens, so write 0 in the tens place.
A big square is 1 hundred. A long rod is 1 ten. A small cube is 1 unit. Count each kind: 3 hundreds, 5 tens, 6 units.
Each rod is 10. There are 6 rods. 6 tens = 60.
A big square is 1 hundred. A long rod is 1 ten. A small cube is 1 unit. Count each kind: 4 hundreds, 7 tens, 1 unit.

items.q: Which matches the blocks?
items.e: A big square is 1 hundred. A long rod is 1 ten. A small cube is 1 unit. Count each kind: 1 hundred, 2 tens, 7 units.
Count each kind. 1 hundred = 100. 2 tens = 20. 0 units = 0. 100 + 20 = 120. There are no ones, so write 0 in the units place.
Each rod is 10. There are 4 rods. 4 tens = 40.
Fourteen is 1 ten and 4 units, so write 14. Do not mix it up with forty, which is 40.
Forty is 4 tens and 0 units, so write 40. Numbers ending in “ty” are tens. Fourteen is 14.

items.q: How many tens are in seventy-two?
items.e: Seventy-two is 72: 7 tens and 2 units. There are 7 tens.
Sixty-three is 6 tens and 3 units, so write 63. Do not write 603: a 2-digit number has only 2 digits.

items.q: Which shows the number in words?
items.e: 2 rods and 7 cubes: 2 tens and 7 units = 27. In words: twenty-seven.
Eighteen is 1 ten and 8 units, so write 18. Do not mix it up with eighty, which is 80.

items.q: Which place tells you which number is greater?
items.e: Look at the hundreds first. 413 has 4 hundreds and 375 has 3 hundreds. 4 > 3, so 413 > 375. The tens and units do not matter. So Kano tell you which number is greater.

items.q: Which place tells you which number is greater?
items.e: Both have 4 hundreds. Look at the tens next. 415 has 1 ten and 434 has 3 tens. 1 < 3, so 415 < 434. The ones do not matter. So Abuja tell you which number is greater.

items.q: Which place tells you which number is greater?
items.e: Both have 2 hundreds and 4 tens. Look at the units. 246 has 6 units and 248 has 8 units. 6 < 8, so 246 < 248. So Lagos tell you which number is greater.

items.q: Which place tells you which number is greater?
items.e: Both have 3 hundreds. Look at the tens next. 307 has 0 tens and 370 has 7 tens. 0 < 7, so 307 < 370. The ones do not matter. So Abuja tell you which number is greater.

items.q: Which place tells you which number is greater?
items.e: Look at the hundreds first. 302 has 3 hundreds and 217 has 2 hundreds. 3 > 2, so 302 > 217. The tens and units do not matter. So Kano tell you which number is greater.

items.q: Which place tells you which number is greater?
items.e: Both have 1 hundred. Look at the tens next. 174 has 7 tens and 107 has 0 tens. 7 > 0, so 174 > 107. The ones do not matter. So Abuja tell you which number is greater.
The numbers are 264, 246, 300 and 290. Hundreds first: 2, 2, 3 and 2. 2 is the smallest. Tens of 264, 246 and 290: 6, 4 and 9. 4 is the smallest. So 246 is the least.
Write each one as a number: 510, 490, 190 and 501. Hundreds first: 5, 4, 1 and 5. 5 is the biggest. Tens of 510 and 501: 1 and 0. 1 is the biggest. So 5 hundreds 1 ten (510) is the greatest.
Write each one as a number: 320, 290, 302 and 209. Hundreds first: 3, 2, 3 and 2. 2 is the smallest. Tens of 290 and 209: 9 and 0. 0 is the smallest. So 2 hundreds 9 units (209) is the least.

items.q: Which place tells you which number is greater?
items.e: Look at the hundreds first. 423 has 4 hundreds and 376 has 3 hundreds. 4 > 3, so 423 > 376. The tens and units do not matter. So Kano tell you which number is greater.

items.q: Which place tells you which number is greater?
items.e: Both have 1 hundred. Look at the tens next. 125 has 2 tens and 130 has 3 tens. 2 < 3, so 125 < 130. The ones do not matter. So Abuja tell you which number is greater.

items.q: Which place tells you which number is greater?
items.e: Both have 2 hundreds and 3 tens. Look at the units. 234 has 4 units and 239 has 9 units. 4 < 9, so 234 < 239. So Lagos tell you which number is greater.

items.q: Which place tells you which number is greater?
items.e: Both have 4 hundreds. Look at the tens next. 407 has 0 tens and 470 has 7 tens. 0 < 7, so 407 < 470. The ones do not matter. So Abuja tell you which number is greater.

items.q: Which place tells you which number is greater?
items.e: Look at the hundreds first. 116 has 1 hundred and 238 has 2 hundreds. 1 < 2, so 116 < 238. So Kano tell you which number is greater.
60 is 6 tens. 4 is 4 units. 6 tens and 4 units = 64. Not 604.
47 is 4 tens and 7 units. 4 tens = 40. So 47 = 40 + 7.
63 is 6 tens and 3 units. 6 tens = 60, not 6. So 63 = 60 + 3.

items.q: Which shows 72 split into tens and units?
items.e: 72 is 7 tens and 2 units. 7 tens = 70. So 72 = 70 + 2.
50 is 5 tens and 7 is 7 units. Tens come first: 57. The order you add them does not matter.
85 is 8 tens and 5 units. 85 = 80 + 5.

items.q: Which shows 38 split into tens and units?
items.e: 38 is 3 tens and 8 units. 3 tens = 30. So 38 = 30 + 8.
29 is 2 tens and 9 units. 2 tens = 20. So 20 + 9 = 29.

items.q: Which shows 56 split into tens and units?
items.e: 56 is 5 tens and 6 units. 5 tens = 50. So 56 = 50 + 6.
8 tens = 80. There are 0 units, so the number is 80.

items.q: There are 3 tens and 17 units. What number is it?
items.e: 3 tens = 30. 17 units = 1 ten and 7 units. So 30 + 17 = 47.
26 can be 1 ten and 16 units. 10 + 16 = 26. (6 is wrong: 10 + 6 = 16.)

items.q: ☐ + 50 + 6 = 156. What number goes in the box?
items.e: The hundreds digit of 156 is 1. Its value is 100. Check: 100 + 50 + 6 = 156.
3 + 100 = 103. Put each part in its place: 1 hundred, 0 tens, 3 units. Start with the hundreds, even if they come last.
100 + 30 = 130. Put each part in its place: 1 hundred, 3 tens, 0 units.

items.q: 100 + 90 + ☐ = 197. What number goes in the box?
items.e: The units digit of 197 is 7. Its value is 7. Check: 100 + 90 + 7 = 197.
100 + 60 = 160. Put each part in its place: 1 hundred, 6 tens, 0 units.

items.q: ☐ + 90 + 7 = 197. What number goes in the box?
items.e: The hundreds digit of 197 is 1. Its value is 100. Check: 100 + 90 + 7 = 197.

items.q: ☐ + 90 + 3 = 193. What number goes in the box?
items.e: The hundreds digit of 193 is 1. Its value is 100. Check: 100 + 90 + 3 = 193.
Look at the tens first. 74 has 7 tens and 47 has 4 tens. So 74 > 47. The open side of the sign faces the bigger number.

items.q: What number does the arrow point to?
items.e: From 0 to 100 there are 10 jumps, so each mark is 10. Count in tens from 0: 10, 20, 30.
Compare the tens first, then the units. In order: 29, 45, 68, 71. The greatest is 71. 29 has the biggest units digit, but only 2 tens.
Numbers between 30 and 40 have 3 tens: 31, 32, … 39. 34 has 3 tens, so it fits.

items.q: What number does the arrow point to?
items.e: From 0 to 100 there are 10 jumps, so each mark is 10. Count in tens from 0: 10, 20, 30, 40, 50, 60, 70, 80.
Compare the tens first, then the units. In order: 35, 39, 50, 53. The smallest is 35.

items.q: Put 56, 65, 46 in order from smallest to greatest.
items.e: Compare the tens first. If the tens are the same, compare the units. From smallest to greatest: 46, 56, 65.

items.q: Estimate the number the arrow points to.
items.e: Each mark is 10. The arrow is halfway between 40 and 50. Halfway is 45.

items.q: Put 73, 37, 70 in order from greatest to smallest.
items.e: Compare the tens first. If the tens are the same, compare the units. From greatest to smallest: 73, 70, 37.
Numbers between 60 and 70 have 6 tens: 61, 62, … 69. 67 has 6 tens, so it fits.
Look at the tens first. 52 has 5 tens and 49 has 4 tens. So 52 > 49. Do not look at the units first: 9 units is less than 1 ten. The open side of the sign faces the bigger number.
Look at the tens first. 83 has 8 tens and 38 has 3 tens. So 83 > 38. The open side of the sign faces the bigger number.
Look at the tens first. 61 has 6 tens and 16 has 1 ten. So 61 > 16. The open side of the sign faces the bigger number.
Compare the tens first, then the units. In order: 80, 89, 90, 98. The greatest is 98.
30 + 6 is 3 tens and 6 units, which is 36. Both sides are the same, so use =.

items.q: Estimate the number the arrow points to.
items.e: The arrow is halfway between 0 and 50, so it is about 25. 75 is halfway between 50 and 100.
Compare the tens first, then the units. In order: 12, 19, 21, 91. The smallest is 12. 19 and 12 both have 1 ten. 2 units < 9 units.
Fourteen is 14 (1 ten). Forty is 40 (4 tens). 14 < 40.

items.q: What number does the arrow point to?
items.e: Each mark is 1. Count on from 45: 46, 47. The arrow shows 47.

items.q: Put 18, 81, 80 in order from smallest to greatest.
items.e: Compare the tens first. If the tens are the same, compare the units. From smallest to greatest: 18, 80, 81.
